dials._note: Design 15 B2: the personality dials, as pictures. One letter per pixel, space = clear. A doll shows at most two of them, and only the ones that are not middling.

bodyLooks._note: His note, 4 Oct 2026 (nothing happens when I place the sheep costume): a costume worn on the body is seen on a person, on the field and on her card, as the person's own sprite with these letters recoloured (b the shirt, n the hair, N the shoes; render.js spriteOf, doll.js). A body piece with no look here shows only on her card.

hats._note: Hats drawn over a creature's head (gear effect hat): [palette letter, x, y, w, h] in its 8x8 sprite, y 0 = the top row.

glyphs._note: Marks drawn over a creature (design 14 §6): huh = an attack the harm table blocked (the attacker shows ?), warn = a hazard that will hurt it soon (!), z = asleep (design 18 A5). # = the mark, drawn with a dark outline; the z alone is drawn twice, rising, with a one pixel shadow and no outline (F3: in a 3x5 pixel font a Z IS a 2, and a heavy outline merged it into a dark badge).

saveIcon._note: The disk that pulses in the corner of the menu button when a save lands (design 14 §7 T1). One letter per pixel, space = clear.

findArrow._note: Design 19 A6 (the locator): the one arrow at the field's edge while her finger is down on a name and the one on the card is off the screen (main.js find). # = the arrow, in col, with a one pixel outline in glyphs.outline; px points east and diag south east, and each is turned a quarter at a time for the other six ways (never at a slant, so its pixels stay square). ui.locator.arrowPx says how big a pixel is.

_edgeMix: Ground meets ground along a coast, not a ruled line: how many pixels deep a tile may borrow its neighbour colour. The DEPTH varies along the edge (a fixed depth draws a dotted halo and makes the rectangle more legible, not less). Length is the maximum depth; [] or absent = hard edges, the way it was.

cardArt._note: His cards (1 and 2 Oct 2026; src/ui/cardart.js, the lead's draft THE CARD LOOK): each section of the Scrapbook's cards is a frame in its own colour (base, light: the bevel's lit side, dark: its shaded side) with a little pattern (motif: rows of x and ., repeated round all four sides); deck is the back of a card she has not turned yet. ink: the frame's outline, and the soft edge drawn round an animal on a card so a white one shows on the ice (inkAlpha). hours: the light laid over a card's picture at that hour (none by day; nightCast: how bright the animals stay at night).

chips._note: Card polish 3 (3 Oct 2026; src/ui/chips.js): the chip under every picture a strip draws (her news line, the answer over it, Today, a card's strip, the sparkle's card). A picture sits on the first of tiles (terrain ids: the chip is the tile's first colour) where it reads: at least share of its pixels, and share of its outline, stand out from the chip by dE or more (CIE76). Design 18 F4's grass first; the sand for the pictures that are the grass's own green (the frog, the snake, the cactus, the reeds, the palm). The law: fixture every-picture-reads-on-its-chip.
